title: Provision and Landfall
premise: Salvage diver Rosalind Reyes is hired to strip a wrecked naval transport the government officially denies ever existed, and among its ballast she recovers the body of a prospector clutching a map to the river's forbidden source — a valley the state flooded decades ago to bury a massacre and its gold. The prospector's dying promise binds her to deliver the map to his estranged daughter, but the navy's salvage officer, Commander Hale, will kill to keep the valley's truth drowned, and the daughter, Ines, wants justice more than she wants to survive. Rosalind, who has spent seven years drifting to avoid belonging anywhere, must choose between the loyalty she owes the dead man and the truth that could destroy the only family she's ever been offered. She leads Ines upriver past Hale's patrols, reaches the source as the dry season closes the channels, and forces the floodgates open — drowning the navy's cover-up in evidence and claiming, at last, a place to stand.
about_author: Rafael Crane is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade diving wrecks across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people who measure their lives in distances rather than years.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Deny
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working the unmarked wreck off a navy-restricted coast, she finds the drowned prospector and his waterproofed map, and hears his last words: a promise owed to a daughter named Ines. When Commander Hale arrives to seize 'naval property,' Rosalind hides the map and lies to his face. Emotional beat: the first pull of obligation in seven years of deliberate drift.

chapters.title: A Debt in Dry Season
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tracks Ines to a river town and delivers the map, but Hale's men are already asking questions, and Ines reveals the valley was flooded to bury a massacre her father witnessed. With the dry season shrinking the river channels daily, they hire a battered boat and a crew of outcasts who owe Rosalind old debts. Emotional beat: loyalty crystallizing into commitment.

chapters.title: Upstream of the Law
chapters.summary: Alternating Rosalind and Ines POV. The ascent becomes a gauntlet: Hale's patrol boat shadows them, a crew member sells them out, and a night ambush forces Rosalind to choose saving the map or saving Ines — she chooses Ines, nearly losing everything. Ines confesses she wants the gold as much as the truth. Emotional beat: trust forged under fire, and the cost of honesty between allies.

chapters.title: Landfall at the Source
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the last navigable hours before the river fails, they reach the drowned valley and dive the flooded village, recovering the massacre's records and gold as Hale closes in. Rosalind opens the spillway, letting the evidence wash downstream to the press waiting at the delta, while Hale's own men, shown the truth, stand down. Emotional beat: a woman who measured life in miles finally plants her feet in one place — and belongs.
